matthew.27.p1.b1.text: When morning came, all the chief priests and elders of the people conspired against Jesus to put Him to death.

matthew.27.p1.b2.text: They bound Him, led Him away,

matthew.27.p1.b3.text: and handed Him over to Pilate the governor.

matthew.27.p2.b1.text: When Judas, who had betrayed Him, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was filled with remorse

matthew.27.p2.b2.text: and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders.

matthew.27.p2.b3.text: I have sinned by betraying innocent blood

matthew.27.p2.b4.text: What is that to us? … You bear the responsibility.

matthew.27.p3.b1.text: So Judas threw the silver into the temple and left.

matthew.27.p3.b2.text: Then he went away and hanged himself.

matthew.27.p3.b3.text: It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money.

matthew.27.p4.b1.text: After conferring together, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.

matthew.27.p4.b2.text: That is why it has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

matthew.27.p4.b3.text: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:

matthew.27.p4.b4.text: They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on Him … and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord had commanded me.

matthew.27.p5.b1.text: Meanwhile Jesus stood before the governor, who questioned Him:

matthew.27.p5.b2.text: Are You the King of the Jews?

matthew.27.p5.b4.text: Do You not hear how many charges they are bringing against You?

matthew.27.p6.b1.text: Now it was the governor’s custom at the feast to release to the crowd a prisoner of their choosing.

matthew.27.p6.b2.text: At that time they were holding a notorious prisoner named Barabbas.

matthew.27.p6.b3.text: Which one do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?

matthew.27.p6.b4.text: For he knew it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over to him.

matthew.27.p7.b1.text: While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him this message:

matthew.27.p7.b2.text: Have nothing to do with that innocent man,

matthew.27.p7.b3.text: for I have suffered terribly in a dream today because of Him.

matthew.27.p8.b1.text: But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.

matthew.27.p8.b2.text: Which of the two do you want me to release to you?

matthew.27.p8.b4.text: What then should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?

matthew.27.p8.b5.text: Why? … What evil has He done?

matthew.27.p9.b1.text: When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that instead a riot was breaking out, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd.

matthew.27.p9.b2.text: I am innocent of this man’s blood … You bear the responsibility.

matthew.27.p9.b3.text: His blood be on us and on our children!

matthew.27.p10.b1.text: So Pilate released Barabbas to them.

matthew.27.p10.b3.text: and handed Him over to be crucified.

matthew.27.p11.b1.text: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium and gathered the whole company around Him.

matthew.27.p11.b2.text: They stripped Him and put a scarlet robe on Him.

matthew.27.p11.b4.text: Then they spit on Him and took the staff and struck Him on the head repeatedly.

matthew.27.p12.b1.text: After they had mocked Him, … put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him away to crucify Him.

matthew.27.p12.b2.text: Along the way they found a man from Cyrene, … and they forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.

matthew.27.p12.b3.text: And when they came to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull,

matthew.27.p12.b4.text: they offered Him wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, He refused to drink it.

matthew.27.p13.b1.text: When they had crucified Him, they divided up His garments by casting lots.

matthew.27.p13.b2.text: And sitting down, they kept watch over Him there.

matthew.27.p13.b3.text: Above His head they posted the written charge against Him: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

matthew.27.p13.b4.text: Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right hand and the other on His left.

matthew.27.p14.b1.text: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads

matthew.27.p14.b2.text: You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself!

matthew.27.p14.b3.text: If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!

matthew.27.p15.b1.text: He saved others, but He cannot save Himself.

matthew.27.p15.b2.text: He is the King of Israel! Let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.

matthew.27.p15.b3.text: He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”

matthew.27.p15.b4.text: In the same way, even the robbers who were crucified with Him berated Him.

matthew.27.p16.b1.text: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.

matthew.27.p16.b3.text: My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?

matthew.27.p17.b1.text: One of them quickly ran and brought a sponge. He filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and held it up for Jesus to drink.

matthew.27.p17.b2.text: Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.

matthew.27.p17.b3.text: When Jesus had cried out again in a loud voice,

matthew.27.p18.b1.text: At that moment the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

matthew.27.p18.b2.text: The earth quaked and the rocks were split.

matthew.27.p18.b3.text: The tombs broke open, and the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised.

matthew.27.p18.b4.text: After Jesus’ resurrection, when they had come out of the tombs, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.

matthew.27.p19.b1.text: When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and all that had happened, they were terrified and said,

matthew.27.p19.b2.text: Truly this was the Son of God.

matthew.27.p19.b3.text: And many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to Him.

matthew.27.p19.b4.text: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.

matthew.27.p20.b1.text: When it was evening, there came a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph,

matthew.27.p20.b2.text: who himself was a disciple of Jesus.

matthew.27.p20.b3.text: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus,

matthew.27.p20.b4.text: and Pilate ordered that it be given to him.

matthew.27.p21.b1.text: So Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,

matthew.27.p21.b2.text: and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut into the rock.

matthew.27.p21.b3.text: Then he rolled a great stone across the entrance to the tomb and went away.

matthew.27.p22.b1.text: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting there

matthew.27.p23.b1.text: The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees assembled before Pilate.

matthew.27.p23.b2.text: “Sir,” they said, “we remember that while He was alive that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise again.’

matthew.27.p23.b3.text: So give the order that the tomb be secured until the third day. Otherwise, His disciples may come and steal Him away

matthew.27.p23.b4.text: And this last deception would be worse than the first.

matthew.27.p24.b1.text: You have a guard … Go, make the tomb as secure as you know how.

matthew.27.p24.b2.text: So they went and secured the tomb
